info.title: Starfleet Assets service
info.summary: Read-only REST/JSON catalogue of starships, shuttles, ground vehicles and equipment.
info.description: Contract 1.1 of the Assets bounded context. It follows 1.0 and makes two changes: the asset identifier is now native to Assets (AST-0017, not the Missions-style SH-17), and a path outside the two paths is answered 404 PATH_NOT_FOUND. The service is read-only: it answers GET for one asset and for a filtered, ordered, paginated list, answers every other method on those two paths with 405, and answers a path outside the two with 404 PATH_NOT_FOUND. It owns asset facts only. It stores no location, makes no judgment about time, and never checks the assets that other services reference. The contract version is MAJOR.MINOR: a breaking change is a new major, a new component and a new endpoint; a compatible addition is a new minor published as a new immutable file. This file is never edited after publication, and neither is the 1.0 file beside it. The change of the identifier grammar would normally be a new major; it is made in 1.1 because 1.0 never had a consumer. See docs/ASSETS-V1-DESIGN.md.

get.summary: List assets, filtered, ordered and paginated.
get.description: Filters (kind, category, status, parentAssetId) combine with AND; each takes exactly one token. Order is assetId ascending: the letter prefix first, then the numeric suffix as a number, so AST-0002 comes before AST-0017 and AST-9999 before AST-10000. Totals are counted after filtering. An offset at or beyond the total returns an empty items array and is not an error. An unknown query parameter, a repeated parameter or an invalid value is 400 INVALID_REQUEST. A parentAssetId filter that names no asset is not an error and selects nothing. The list is a live view: there is no snapshot between requests.

200.description: One page of assets, possibly empty.

page.summary: A page of three assets out of thirty-one.

vehicles.summary: The category filter: category=VEHICLE lists starships, shuttles, rovers and armored vehicles.

beyondEnd.summary: The offset is past the last asset: empty items, the total still reported.

get.description: Any asset that exists answers 200 with its record, whatever its status: ACTIVE, MAINTENANCE, DECOMMISSIONED, DESTROYED and MISSING all resolve, and the service judges none of them. A well-formed identifier that names no asset is 404 ASSET_NOT_FOUND. A malformed identifier is 400 INVALID_ASSET_ID, and so is an identifier in the old Missions grammar (SH-17). The identifier is validated exactly as sent, with no case folding, trimming or other normalization.

starshipActive.summary: A starship in service, with no parent.

equipmentAboard.summary: Equipment aboard a starship: the parent is the starship.

equipmentAboardRover.summary: Equipment aboard a rover: any VEHICLE can be a parent.

roverActive.summary: A ground exploration rover in service.

armoredVehicleActive.summary: An armored ground vehicle built for combat.

equipmentDecommissioned.summary: Equipment retired in the normal way.

shuttleDestroyed.summary: A destroyed shuttle still resolves, with its status and its parent.

equipmentMissing.summary: Equipment whose whereabouts are unknown still resolves, with its status.

musicalInstrumentActive.summary: A musical instrument is a plain asset like any other.

x-unmatchedPath.description: A path outside the two paths above, whatever the method, is 404 PATH_NOT_FOUND. The code is distinct from ASSET_NOT_FOUND on purpose: ASSET_NOT_FOUND means one thing only, a well-formed asset lookup that found nothing, so a client that built a wrong path is never mistaken for one that looked up a missing asset.

AssetId.description: A native asset identifier: a system prefix, a hyphen and a zero-padded number, for example AST-0017. The prefix is one to three segments of capital letters joined by single underscores (the first segment 2 to 8 letters, the others 1 to 8); it never starts or ends with an underscore. The number is at least four digits, never all zeros, with one canonical spelling: four digits with leading zeros up to 9999, and from 10000 on no leading zeros. Every asset of the dataset uses the prefix AST; the grammar allows other prefixes for the future. The prefix carries no meaning: the kind is a field of the asset. This is not the grammar of the asset references of the Missions contract (SH-17 and the like): those are Missions-local, and mapping one to an Assets identifier belongs to the integration layer, not to this contract.

AssetKind.description: What kind of asset this is. STARSHIP: a starship, a large crewed ship such as the Enterprise. SHUTTLE: a small craft that flies between ships and surfaces; a runabout counts as a SHUTTLE until a scenario needs a separate kind. ROVER: a ground exploration vehicle. ARMORED_VEHICLE: Land-based vehicles built for active combat zones and mechanized warfare (an armored ground vehicle built for combat, tracked or wheeled). PHASER: a hand-held energy weapon. TRICORDER: a hand-held scanner and recorder. COMMUNICATOR: a personal communication device such as a comm badge. SCIENTIFIC_INSTRUMENT: an instrument for measurement, analysis or research that is not a tricorder. MUSICAL_INSTRUMENT: an instrument for making music, such as a flute, a violin or a trombone. Every asset fits a named kind: there is no generic kind. A new kind is one enum value and one row of the kind-to-category table: a compatible minor change.

AssetCategory.description: The category of an asset, derived from its kind and never stored apart from it: STARSHIP, SHUTTLE, ROVER and ARMORED_VEHICLE are VEHICLE; PHASER, TRICORDER, COMMUNICATOR, SCIENTIFIC_INSTRUMENT and MUSICAL_INSTRUMENT are EQUIPMENT. Only a VEHICLE can be a parent. The contract cannot state that the category agrees with the kind; the validator checks it and the design document owns the table.

AssetStatus.description: ACTIVE and MAINTENANCE describe an asset in the fleet. DECOMMISSIONED is a normal retirement. DESTROYED is confirmed and final: the asset cannot return. MISSING means the whereabouts are unknown: the asset can return to ACTIVE if it is found.

name.description: The asset's name, 1 to 120 Unicode code points.

description.description: Free text, 1 to 1000 Unicode code points.

parentAssetId.description: The asset this one is aboard or part of, or null when it has none. Always present. A parent that is named exists in this service: it is a database foreign key, so a dangling parent cannot occur. Only an asset whose category is VEHICLE can be a parent; the contract cannot express that rule between records, so the design document states it.

Asset.description: One asset. category is computed from kind by the kind-to-category table of the design document: a record whose category disagrees with its kind is invalid.

total.description: How many assets match the filters, counted before paging.

message.description: Human-readable text, 1 to 1000 Unicode code points. Never a stack trace or framework detail, and not meant to be parsed: the HTTP status and the code are the contract.

CategoryFilter.name: category
CategoryFilter.description: Select assets of this category: VEHICLE or EQUIPMENT. Exactly one token.

ParentAssetIdFilter.name: parentAssetId
ParentAssetIdFilter.description: Select the assets whose parent is this asset, for example the equipment aboard a starship.

Offset.name: offset
Offset.description: How many matching assets to skip. Canonical decimal text: 0, 20, 100; never 00, +5 or 1.5. The default is 0.

Limit.name: limit
Limit.description: The most assets to return, 1 to 50, in canonical decimal text. The default is 20.

Allow.description: The only method the path supports.

InvalidRequest.description: 400 INVALID_REQUEST: an invalid recognized query value, an unknown query parameter or a repeated parameter.

InvalidAssetId.description: 400 INVALID_ASSET_ID: the identifier in the path does not match the asset grammar.

AssetNotFound.description: 404 ASSET_NOT_FOUND: the identifier is well formed and no asset has it.

assetNotFound.summary: A well-formed identifier that names nothing.

PathNotFound.description: 404 PATH_NOT_FOUND: the path is outside the two paths of this contract, whatever the method. It is never ASSET_NOT_FOUND, which means a well-formed asset lookup that found nothing.

MethodNotAllowed.description: 405 METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED: the service is read-only; every method but GET is refused, with an Allow header.

InternalError.description: 500 INTERNAL_ERROR: an unexpected server or database failure.
